Image 1 is a photo of a room. Images 2 to 7 are products, one photo each:
image 2: medium-height open bookcase, 80 cm wide
image 3: cantilever bentwood leather lounge armchair, size unknown
image 4: round shaggy high-pile rug, size unknown
image 5: swing-arm floor lamp with drum shade, size unknown
image 6: organic-shaped nesting tables, size unknown
image 7: pair of linen curtains, size unknown

The person asked for this room: "Quiero un amoblado acogedor que combine con el tono amaderado del suelo. Quisiera una estantería para mis libros en la pared, una alfombra circular en el suelo y algún lugar para sentarme a leer."

Furnish the room in image 1 with these products, as an interior designer would for that request. You decide where each product goes and how the room is arranged. Use every product. Furniture that comes in units, like bookcases and shelves, can be repeated side by side to fill a wall, the way the store sells it; give every piece its real size against the room.

Keep image 1 as it is: the same framing and camera, walls, floor, ceiling, windows and light. Only add the products, each with the design, proportions, colors and materials of its photo, lit like the room. The result must look like a real photograph.
